author: Warren
text:
All,

I have been very much a S & D trader, ever since meeting RED on PIE thread. I do love my engulfs, but i know it is only part of the story.

Good money management and the right psychology have kept me in the green. 5 years of account growth has meant, lot sizes can yield some nice returns on even small moves. It has got to the stage where i know i must drop the rectangle box indi and come away from S & D thinking, it is working against the method before me. If ever i am going to reach enlightenment i must move forward.

With total honesty i can not see some of the things you guys point out,, i have this badge that should not be mine, until i prove myself at "Reading Price" It is now starting to bug me, so i am putting my hands up "can not do this yet"

I am going back to raw basics and will go through all the homework sections,i know some sections i will breeze through others i will struggle at first. It seems my Psychology threads put me in a place i should not be.

Yes, i have done very well out of trading, but this puzzle is nagging me to death, and i cant see it "whole". Until i prove otherwise i will not be comfortable with myself, i only have part of the story. Success.........Define success.

IF,

I have a request, in fact i must insist. Thank you for thinking so highly of me to award me the badge, you know since that day it has bugged me.

Will you place me back at the FIRST rank where it all starts. I need to start my journey again, you will be honoring my wish as a friend and my mentor.

I haven't gone mad, lost my Wife, had a margin call or anything so extreme. Just a long hard honest look in the mirror!

author: Alientrader
text: Hello Warren, Not sure if I'm even welcome here at RTM anymore but I confess I visit often. Your thread is always top of my list to read. I was moved by your request to "demote" yourself. Having gone through a very uncertain and sometimes down-right depressing period in my trading I in many ways accidentally came back to s/d trading. At first I kind of didn't like to even call it that because it was so entrenched in the supply and demand ZONE mantra. S/D trading is not really so much about finding these S/D zones although there is some validity in that. There is more to it. I have a thread at FF (the engulf method) that I started from scratch because of plain old observations that I was making about the market. As I traded this method it dawned on me that I was actually trading s/d again. At first I was reluctant to call it that but now I know that is exactly what it is. Realizing what I was really doing I revisited RTM and read everything in marketpedia again. There was some new stuff that I hadn't seen before and after reading it again and the new stuff many things began to fall in place. I still like to trade the higher time frames with H4 being my favorite but I will drop to LTFs sometimes. don't claim to have figured it all out but I have come full circle and I am profitable in a small way. I keep a trade explorer on FF that documents all my trades on a live account. Stepping away was the best thing I ever did. Coming back was even better. wish you luck Warren. All the best, Winston

author: madwt
text:
Warren wrote: Madwt,

I am seeing quite a lot of reactions to FL's that i never could see before, i will bear this in mind when i attack the FL section.

Many rbr,dbr,dbd....etc are a reaction to a past FL.

I am aware of and understand all the concepts such as support and resistance, supply and demand, RDR, RBD, DBD, DBR, FL, FTR, QM, can can, etc. However, all I am now really seeing on the charts is decisions made on price and each of the for mentioned patterns and price constructs are merely different manifestations of that. I believe that what is critical is to see where the decisions are made and what the decision was a reaction to; and when price decides to break through a previous decision on price (engulf), what happens after. If price continues in the direction of the engulf, a FTR is made. Understanding FO is also critical - why, where and how they form.

In answer your question on whether the blue box with etc is an FTR with a FTB close to the end, it is, although not a 'good' one. Why it is technically an FTR is shown below.

author: Warren
text:
Guy's and Girls,

The time has come where i depart from RTM.

There is no easy way to say it, i have enjoyed my time here but i need to move on. I guess some bright spark will have to add to my threads and carry on where i left off!

I like to think i have come away with more of an understanding and that in turn i have left something behind that new visitors will see. You all know i like to keep it K.I.S.S, and looking at the last year and further back, i just dont feel the urge to push myself for better. Where does it all end? I just need to rinse and repeat often for maximum results.

They say the market is simple, it is, if you find "your kind of simple"

I wish you all well with your journey, because there are many twists and turns. Think logic at all times and keep the MM on side. The answers are all out there, but only you can see it. Look in the mirror.............go on......right NOW! There is your "HOLY GRAIL"
